as_told.title: War of the Worlds broadcast panic

plain: After the Second World War, the theory goes, officials kept UFO matters secret partly because they remembered the panic over The War of the Worlds. That was Orson Welles's radio drama of a Martian invasion, which some listeners took for real news. A former Senate staffer named Kurt McConnell puts it this way: in the postwar years "we were barely a decade removed from Orson Wells War of the Worlds event. I think that was in 1938." John S. Herrington, a former US Secretary of Energy, says the same thing from his time in government: "Orson Wells broadcast war of the world and the country went nuts." Both tell it to explain why leaders might have feared how the public would react to news of UFOs.
